name: Kalbak-Tash Petroglyphs
full: Kalbak-Tash tract — a sanctuary with petroglyphs on the right bank of the Chuya, km 723 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway), between the villages of Inya and Iodro
near: Inya village (≈18–20 km to the west), Iodro village (≈12 km to the east, per Sayan Ring)
short: The largest petroglyph complex in Gorny Altai, right by the Chuysky Trakt: 3,000–5,000 rock carvings from the Neolithic to the Old Turkic era and the largest Old Turkic runic inscription in Russia.
desc: Kalbak-Tash (“flat/hanging stone”) is a tract on the right bank of the Chuya about 10 km from its confluence with the Katun, at km 723 of the Chuysky Trakt (R256 highway). Rock outcrops with carvings stretch along the valley for ≈10 km (km 717–726), and the main exhibition is fenced off and developed by the highway. It was discovered in 1912 by the artists G. I. Choros-Gurkin and D. I. Kuznetsov and has been studied systematically since the 1980s. Estimates range from ≈3,000 to more than 5,000 images (figures differ), aged from 2,500 to 6,000–8,000 years: Neolithic animals, Bronze Age people, warriors, domestic animals, Scythian scenes of hunting ibex and big cats, and Old Turkic inscriptions of the 9th–10th centuries. Among the well-known images are the “Altai chimera”, the sanctuary of the goddess Umay, the “celestial ibex”, the only depiction of an ancient boat in Altai, and mysterious figures in “helmets” with “tails” (they are sometimes passed off as “aliens”; scholars see shamans or priestesses). The runic inscription — about 30 lines — is considered the largest Old Turkic one in Russia. On the site there are wooden railings and information signs; entry is paid, and local guides work here. The site lies within the boundaries of the former Chuy-Oozy nature park — people navigate by the sign for it.
guide: Be sure to take a local guide at the entrance: without one you'll see only “scribbles” in the cracks of the rocks, and with one — deer, the chimera and hunting scenes. Look for the “aliens” in helmets — it's a popular riddle at Kalbak-Tash, and guides love to solve it. Come in the morning or toward evening: in side light the carvings are much easier to read than at noon. There are three “stones” on the site — a female one, a male one and a wish-granting one; touch only those, not the petroglyphs. Bring cash — there may be no card terminal.
see: The main fenced-off exhibition with a trail; the Old Turkic runic inscription (~30 lines); the Umay sanctuary; the “Altai chimera”; the “celestial ibex”; the depiction of a boat; sun signs and a “star map”; figures in “helmets”; wish stones; a view of the Chuya valley.
skip: You're not interested in archaeology and aren't ready to take a guide: without explanations the carvings are hard to make out, and the visit turns into a walk over rocks. It's hard on the open rocks in the hot midday.
diff: Easy: a walk over rocks and a trail for 1–3 h, small climbs
when: May–October (guides work); spring and autumn are more comfortable temperature-wise. In winter the site is accessible, but the carvings may be under snow (not confirmed).
hours: According to 2GIS reviews: 9:00–17:00 (September 2024); in February 2025 — “closed on schedule” (the ticket office may be closed in winter); in April 2026 — open, entry paid, with a guided tour. Blogs give 8:00–21:00 (Turister, Sayan Ring, Snovatrip). Phone on 2GIS: +7 983 327-82-17 (the data has not been updated for a long time).
daytime: Morning and early evening — slanting light makes the carvings stand out more (editorial note)
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to km 723 — the sign of the Chuy-Oozy nature and economic park: ≈288–290 km from Gorno-Altaysk (≈4.5 h), ≈376 km from Biysk. The Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus) (09:00) goes past — ask to be stopped at Kalbak-Tash.
self: Yes (entry is paid, the guide is optional; according to Sibalt-2023 a guide was mandatory — check)
roadtype: Paved R-256, parking by the highway; on the site — a trail over rocks
traveltime: ≈4.5 h from Gorno-Altaysk; ≈1.5 h from Ongudai; ≈15 min from the confluence
stay: The nearest are the holiday camps in Inya (Chetyre Bogatyrya from 3,000 ₽, Alkyshtu from 4,000 ₽) and the Inegen agro-complex; further on — Aktash; Maly Yaloman — Baylyk, Ail (from 2,500 ₽), Baykan on the Katun bank (from 3,000 ₽) — 2GIS 2026
entry: Conflicting data by year: 130 ₽ (Sayan Ring); 150 ₽ + guide 200 ₽ per group (Sibalt, 2023); 200 ₽ + tour 250 ₽ (Turister); 250–300 ₽ + tour 300 ₽, children free, no receipts (2GIS reviews, September–October 2024); April 2026 — entry paid, the guided tour costs ≈50 ₽ more than a regular ticket (2GIS); ≈300 ₽ (Snovatrip, 2026). Rough figure for 2026: ≈300–350 ₽.
transfer: Excursions 8,000–12,900 ₽/person (group tours along the highway), private ones 27,000–45,000 ₽ per vehicle (2026)
bring: Cash (according to reviews, receipts aren't always issued), comfortable shoes, water, a hat, sun protection
warn: Do not touch or trace the carvings, and don't climb the fenced-off rocks — it is a cultural heritage site. It is hot on the open rocks in summer; snakes and ticks are possible (common in Altai). Complaints in reviews: no receipts, litter. R-256 repairs in 2026: in the Altai Republic km 439–444 (Maima) and 560–570 (exit from Shebalino) have been repaired; until the end of 2026 work is under way at km 455–472 (Souzga–Manzherok) and 479–495 (Izvestkovy–Barangol) — lane narrowing and alternating traffic are possible (Tolk, 06.10.2026). In 2026–2029 — reconstruction of 18 km at Souzga–Manzherok with detours (Tolk, 24.03.2026). On 01.10.2026 a rockfall onto the highway with no injuries was reported (NGS22; location not specified). The highway is periodically closed for military convoys. There is no border zone (Ongudai district). Ticks: according to Rospotrebnadzor for the Altai Republic, by 25.08.2026 there were 3,600 reports of tick bites and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (the Ongudai district is among the districts with bites). Card terminals in the villages work unreliably — bring cash (OneTwoTrip, 10.2024).
food: A café on site is mentioned (2GIS review, 10.2024); nearby — the Chuy-Oozy café in Chuyozy village (bill ≈600 ₽, 3.2 on 2GIS) and kiosks at the confluence (yak and maral (Altai red deer) chebureks); in Inya — Kechu, Vkus Altaya
reviews: 2GIS: 4.5 (161–167 ratings, 92–95 reviews, 2024–2026). Pros: “the petroglyphs are simply fire”, strong guides, the energy of the place. Cons: payments without receipts, poor infrastructure, litter.
